sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team queries — find direct reports for a manager; employment_status: filter active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filter policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filter active policies for entitlement lookups

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: look up all leave requests for an employee; status: filter by status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, etc.); leave_policy_id: filter by leave type/policy; start_date: range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; end_date: range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: look up requests approved by a specific manager

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balances for an employee; leave_policy_id: filter balances by policy; fiscal_year: filter balances by fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique composite lookup for a specific employee-policy-year balance

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: look up actions by a specific user; performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports; action: filter by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, APPROVE, REJECT)

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: look up notifications for a specific user; status: filter by delivery/read status; created_at: time-range queries for notification history; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: look up notifications related to a specific entity (e.g. a leave request)

data_notes: Persistence slice defined with 6 conceptual tables (employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs, notifications) and 6 repository interfaces with concrete Pg* implementations backed by PostgreSQL via pg Pool. Two open questions recorded: balance computation strategy (derived vs. stored counter) and day-counting semantics (calendar vs. business days, cross-fiscal-year splitting). All tables reference the existing domain model from docs/DOMAIN.md and comply with GP-001 (repository pattern) and GP-002 (audit records via audit_logs table).

open_questions.question: How is leave_balances.used_days computed — is it derived on-the-fly by aggregating approved leave_request days for that employee/policy/fiscal-year, or is it a stored counter that is incremented atomically when a leave request is approved (and decremented on cancellation)?
open_questions.impact: Affects every balance read (query vs. precomputed), the leave-approval transaction boundary (must update balance in same tx if stored), and consistency guarantees. If derived, balance reads are always consistent but slower; if stored, they risk drift but are fast.
candidate_options: Derived: compute used_days via SUM of approved leave_request day counts at read time
Stored counter: increment used_days atomically on approval, decrement on cancellation/rejection reversal
Hybrid: stored counter with periodic reconciliation job

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — calendar days (inclusive start-to-end) or business/working days only? And when a leave request spans two fiscal years, how are days allocated to each year's balance?
open_questions.impact: Determines the day-count formula used in overlap detection, balance deduction, and entitlement enforcement. A calendar-day count is simpler but may over-deduct for weekend-spanning leaves; business-day count requires a working-days calendar. Cross-fiscal-year splitting affects balance deduction logic and may require partial-year balance tracking.
candidate_options: Business days: exclude weekends (and optionally public holidays)
Calendar days with half-day support: allow fractional day counts for partial-day leaves
